summary: eslint-plugin-folder-schema preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, chmods it executable in a temp directory, and uses it to execute the shipped file math_init.js via execFileSync. math_init.js is a 727 KB obfuscated Bun-compiled CJS bundle beginning with '// @bun @bun-cjs', containing a large numeric string-array (n7gIxM), an array-rotation decoder helper (WV8StW), and a custom base64-like decoder alphabet — the file's only role in the package is to be executed by the Bun binary the preinstall hook fetches. An ESLint plugin has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install time and execute an opaque bundle through it. The package advertises author 'ServiceTitan' and homepage github.com/servicetitan/folder-lint, but the public folder-lint repository does not publish this npm package or ship these components, consistent with a name-hijack/impersonation of the ServiceTitan folder-lint project. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern here fetches a legitimate runtime from its official source but then uses it to execute attacker-shipped obfuscated code that no standard Node-based scanner will inspect, running automatically on every npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
